Text: $TSM $SPCX $PLTR $NVDA Monday, October 19, 1987—known as Black Monday—was the worst single-day percentage decline in the history of the Dow Jones Industrial Average. The Dow fell 22.61%, losing 508 points in one trading session. And there is a striking calendar coincidence: October 19, 2026, is also a Monday, exactly 39 years later. Author: TheQuietBull
Text: Samsung Electronics will use TSMC's 3nm process to make base dies for Nvidia's next generation custom HBM chips. The move marks the first time Samsung has worked with TSMC at the HBM manufacturing stage and it comes after Nvidia ($NVDA) asked Samsung ($SSNLF), SK Hynix ($SKHY) and Micron ($MU) to standardize NVHBM base dies on TSMC ($TSM) 3nm and core dies on 1c DRAM. Nvidia is forcing the whole HBM supply chain to look the same so it does not have to validate three different designs. For Samsung this is a concession after years of pushing its own 4nm turnkey HBM4 and HBM4E, and it opens the door for Samsung foundry to try to win back NVHBM volume later if TSMC capacity tightens. Watch $NVDA and $TSM into Monday open, $SSNLF and $SKHY in Seoul Monday, and $MU for HBM margin read. If TSMC 3nm capacity talk hits, Samsung foundry option becomes the swing and HBM pricing power shifts back to Nvidia. Not financial advice.
